questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A culture I wanted to explore and access to nature. Because of Covid, I did not want to be at a destination very far away if the situation should change. I also wanted to improve my English skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The receiving university did a good job informing me of everything I needed to know.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Everybody is assigned a personal tutor that you meet within the first weeks. I needed some help changing a course and that was solved quickly. I didn´t need more help during the semester, but it was nice to know who to reach out to if I needed help with anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not very easy, but I kept looking and eventually found a room in a private shared flat via Facebook. The university informed me that they didn't guarantee housing for one-semester students so I didn't try to find university accommodation. However, this may have changed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it's cheaper to live off campus. University student accommodation is spread out in the city anyways and Edinburgh is a city where you can walk to most things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't have any problems.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it as you send a request list, they check if you can take the courses, and send an answer with your courses. It was very easy. Just check the course requirements before requesting a course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Visiting Student Office via email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was only registered for courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check requirements. The course searching site is working fine and is easy to use.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was appropriate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The university has tutorial classes where you discuss topics from lectures in smaller groups, often with a Ph.D. student as a tutor. I liked this but unfortunately in my courses, not a lot of students showed up for these.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Dynamics of Language and Power, Linguistics and English Language 1B, Scottish Studies 1B: Creating Scotland

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the Scottish Studies course because I was introduced to many different aspects of Scottish culture.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offers a lot. I joined the fitness center (which has many different classes and a lot of equipment), the futsal club (football), and the book club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just try something, anything. They have so many different options and in the first weeks, many societies host socials where you just show up and see who they are and what they offer.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hikes. Take the bus to the Pentlands or even travel to the Highlands. Isle of Skye is also amazing. And go see lots of castles and ruins, there are quite a few around Edinburgh. Jupiter Artland was also fun. I went to the Lake District in England and to Pembrokeshire in Wales, and can definitely recommend both for hiking if you're looking for longer trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, but I think it's important to get yourself out there in the first weeks and meet some like-minded people to share experiences with.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies or clubs. Go to their socials at the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't really know.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are friendly and down-to-earth. Good humor, mostly. It doesn't feel like a busy place, which was very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join something and meet people through something you like or just try something new. Be very social at the beginning of the semester and relax with good friends later :D Enjoy your city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people. And also, that I've proven to myself that I am able to travel somewhere alone and make it wotk there. That is something I'm definitely bringing with me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe, being exhausted from meeting so many different people, but that is also one of the best things :DD

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
